gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the candidates side by side at the same load: at 500 W the APC SMT1500C runs about 23.1 min against 10 min for the CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD (2.3×), and at 1000 W it runs 6.5 min against 2.5 min (2.6×).
standout_why: I couldn't read most of the rival pages. The SMT1500C datasheets (surveillance-video.com, squarespace, se.com download) and the CyberPower and Tripp Lite datasheet PDFs came back as compressed streams that WebFetch could not decode, and Bash text extraction needed approval I didn't have. cyberpowersystems.com returned 405, B&H and Micro Center returned 403, and eaton.com timed out three times. Each maker datasheet probably gives its own half-load runtime, so the inputs are likely already in the rivals. What none of them can give is the comparison at equal load: each maker rates half load at a different wattage (CyberPower and APC at 500 W, Tripp Lite at 450 W according to search results). ChatGPT's answer doesn't mention runtime at all.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's split between Best overall and Premium and gives the reason for it. The CyberPower gives 10 min at 500 W for $239.99 (Dell), which is enough for a desktop PC to shut down cleanly. The APC's extra cost buys 2.3× the runtime at the same load, which only matters if the shopper needs to ride out outages longer than about 10 minutes. The Tripp Lite can't be placed on the same scale because I couldn't open a page with its runtime figures.
